dialogue.speaker: Khalid
dialogue.arabic: صَبَاحُ الْخَيْر. مَاذَا تُحِبُّ أَنْ تَشْرَب؟
dialogue.transliteration: sabaa7u al-khayr. maadha tu7ibbu an tashrab?
dialogue.english: Good morning. What would you like to drink?

dialogue.speaker: Rami
dialogue.english: Good morning. Coffee, please.

dialogue.speaker: Khalid
dialogue.arabic: كَيْفَ تُحِبُّ قَهْوَتَكَ؟ حُلْوَة أَمْ مُرَّة؟
dialogue.english: How do you like your coffee? Sweet or bitter?

dialogue.speaker: Rami
dialogue.english: I like my coffee bitter, without sugar.

dialogue.speaker: Khalid
dialogue.arabic: وَأَنْتِ يَا لِينَا، مَاذَا تُحِبِّينَ أَنْ تَشْرَبِي؟
dialogue.transliteration: wa anti yaa Leenaa, maadha tu7ibbeena an tashrabee?
dialogue.english: And you, Lina, what would you like to drink?

dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.english: I want mint tea, please.

dialogue.speaker: Khalid
dialogue.english: Certainly. A big cup or a small one?

dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.english: A big cup. Is there sugar?

dialogue.speaker: Khalid
dialogue.english: Yes, here you are. How many spoonfuls do you want?

dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.english: Just one spoonful.

dialogue.speaker: Rami
dialogue.arabic: وَأَنَا أُرِيدُ كُوبًا كَبِيرًا مِنَ الْقَهْوَة.
dialogue.transliteration: wa anaa ureedu koopan kabeeran mina al-qahwa.
dialogue.english: And I want a big cup of coffee.

dialogue.speaker: Khalid
dialogue.english: Fine, two minutes and everything will arrive.

pair.english: What would you like to drink? (to a man)
What would you like to drink? (to a woman)
How do you like your coffee?

lessons.culture: In a Fusha-speaking café the order is polite and short: the drink, then مِنْ فَضْلِكَ. Coffee is usually served in a small cup and offered bitter or sweet, and tea often comes with mint.

exercises.prompt: The waiter says: 'مَاذَا تُحِبُّ أَنْ تَشْرَب؟'. Order a coffee politely.
exercises.tip: Name the drink, then add مِنْ فَضْلِكَ.

exercises.prompt: The waiter asks: 'كَيْفَ تُحِبُّ قَهْوَتَكَ؟'. Say you want it without sugar.
exercises.tip: بِدُونِ means 'without'; it is followed by the thing you leave out.

exercises.prompt: Complete: 'قَهْوَة _____ سُكَّر.' (Coffee with no sugar.)
exercises.tip: بِدُونِ is the everyday word for 'without'.

exercises.prompt: Complete: 'أُرِيدُ _____ بِالنَّعْنَاع.' (I want mint tea.)
exercises.tip: After أُرِيدُ the thing wanted takes the ending ـًا.

exercises.prompt: Translate into Fusha: 'Sweet coffee.'
exercises.tip: The describing word follows the noun and matches it: قَهْوَة حُلْوَة.

exercises.prompt: Translate: 'Is there sugar?'
exercises.tip: هَلْ turns a statement into a yes or no question; يُوجَدُ means 'there is'.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence means 'Tea, please.'?
exercises.tip: شَاي is tea and قَهْوَة is coffee.

exercises.prompt: Which one means 'Coffee with no sugar'?
exercises.tip: بِدُونِ signals that the sugar is left out.

exercises.prompt: Put the pieces in order: 'مِنْ / قَهْوَة، / فَضْلِكَ'.
exercises.tip: The drink first, then the polite ending.

exercises.prompt: Put the pieces in order: 'شَايًا / أُرِيدُ / بِالنَّعْنَاع'.
exercises.tip: Wish first, the drink next, what goes in it last.

phrases.arabic: هَلْ هُوَ حَارّ أَمْ غَيْرُ حَارّ؟

dialogue.speaker: Waiter
dialogue.english: Welcome. Please come in.

dialogue.speaker: Rami
dialogue.english: Thank you. Where is the menu?

dialogue.speaker: Waiter
dialogue.english: Here you are, this is it.

dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.english: Do you have an English menu?

dialogue.speaker: Waiter
dialogue.english: Yes, of course. Here you are.

dialogue.speaker: Rami
dialogue.english: What appetizers do you have?

dialogue.speaker: Waiter
dialogue.english: We have hummus, mutabbal and fattoush.

dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.arabic: هَلْ يُوجَدُ طَعَام نَبَاتِيّ؟ أَنَا لَا آكُلُ اللَّحْم.
dialogue.transliteration: hal yoojadu ta3aam nabaatee? anaa laa aakulu al-la7m.
dialogue.english: Is there vegetarian food? I don't eat meat.

dialogue.speaker: Waiter
dialogue.arabic: نَعَمْ، عِنْدَنَا كَثِير مِنَ الْأَطْبَاقِ النَّبَاتِيَّة.
dialogue.english: Yes, we have many vegetarian dishes.

dialogue.speaker: Rami
dialogue.arabic: مَاذَا فِي هَذَا الطَّبَق؟ وَهَلْ هُوَ حَارّ؟
dialogue.transliteration: maadha fee haadha at-tabaq? wa hal huwa 7aarr?
dialogue.english: What's in this dish? And is it spicy?

dialogue.speaker: Waiter
dialogue.arabic: فِيهِ أُرْز وَخُضَار، وَهُوَ غَيْرُ حَارّ.
dialogue.transliteration: feehi urz wa khudaar, wa huwa ghayru 7aarr.
dialogue.english: It has rice and vegetables, and it is not spicy.

dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.arabic: مَاذَا تَنْصَحُنَا أَنْ نَأْخُذ؟ نُرِيدُ شَيْئًا خَفِيف.
dialogue.transliteration: maadha tansa7unaa an na2khudh? nureedu shay2an khafeef.
dialogue.english: What do you recommend we get? We want something light.

response.english: Here you are, this is it.

pair.arabic: هَلْ هُوَ حَارّ أَمْ غَيْرُ حَارّ؟
pair.english: Is it spicy or not spicy?

lessons.culture: In Fusha the waiter is asked directly and politely, often with هَلْ عِنْدَكُمْ. A request for a recommendation, مَاذَا تَنْصَحُنِي, is welcome in any restaurant.

exercises.prompt: You want the menu. Ask the waiter where it is.
exercises.tip: قَائِمَةُ الطَّعَام is 'the list of food', the menu.

exercises.prompt: The waiter says: 'هَلْ هُوَ حَارّ أَمْ غَيْرُ حَارّ؟'. Answer that it is not spicy.
exercises.tip: غَيْرُ before an adjective makes it negative: 'not spicy'.

exercises.prompt: Complete: 'هَلْ _____ قَائِمَة بِالْإِنْجِلِيزِيَّة؟' (Do you have an English menu?)
exercises.tip: عِنْدَ plus the ending means 'to have'; كُمْ is 'you' for a group.

exercises.prompt: Complete: 'مَاذَا _____ هَذَا الطَّبَق؟' (What's in this dish?)
exercises.tip: فِي means 'in'.

exercises.prompt: Translate into Fusha: 'Do you have desserts?'
exercises.tip: حَلَوِيَّات is the plural, 'sweets' or 'desserts'.

exercises.prompt: Translate: 'I want something light.'
exercises.tip: شَيْئًا is 'something' and خَفِيف is 'light'.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence means 'How much does this cost?'
exercises.tip: بِكَمْ is the everyday way to ask a price.

exercises.prompt: You do not eat meat. Which question do you ask?
exercises.tip: نَبَاتِيّ comes from نَبَات, 'plants'.

exercises.prompt: Put the pieces in order: 'الطَّعَام؟ / أَيْنَ / قَائِمَةُ'.
exercises.tip: The question word first, then what you are looking for.

exercises.prompt: Put the pieces in order: 'تَنْصَحُنِي / مَاذَا / آخُذ؟ / أَنْ'.
exercises.tip: مَاذَا, then the verb 'you advise me', then what to get.

phrases.transliteration: haadha at-tabaqu lee wa haadha lahaa

phrases.arabic: هَلْ يُمْكِنُ أَنْ أَحْصُلَ عَلَى كُوبِ مَاء؟
phrases.transliteration: hal yumkinu an a7sula 3alaa koobi maa2?

dialogue.speaker: Waiter
dialogue.english: Are you ready to order?

dialogue.speaker: Rami
dialogue.english: Yes. I'll have a plate of hummus and fattoush.

dialogue.speaker: Waiter
dialogue.english: Fine. And you, madam?

dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.arabic: أُرِيدُ هَذَا وَهَذَا، بِدُونِ بَصَل، مِنْ فَضْلِكَ.
dialogue.transliteration: ureedu haadha wa haadha, bidooni basal, min fadlika.
dialogue.english: I want this and this, without onion, please.

dialogue.speaker: Waiter
dialogue.english: Certainly. Do you want anything else?

dialogue.speaker: Rami
dialogue.arabic: خُبْز إِضَافِيّ، مِنْ فَضْلِكَ، وَكُوب مَاء.
dialogue.transliteration: khubz idaafee, min fadlika, wa koob maa2.
dialogue.english: Extra bread, please, and a glass of water.

dialogue.speaker: Waiter
dialogue.english: Fine. Is that everything?

dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.arabic: نَعَمْ، شُكْرًا. بِسُرْعَة مِنْ فَضْلِكَ، نَحْنُ جَائِعُونَ.
dialogue.transliteration: na3am, shukran. bisur3a min fadlika, na7nu jaa2i3oon.
dialogue.english: Yes, thanks. Quickly please, we are hungry.

dialogue.speaker: Waiter
dialogue.english: The order will be ready soon.

dialogue.speaker: Rami
dialogue.arabic: لَوْ سَمَحْتَ، لَمْ يَصِلْ طَلَبِي بَعْد.
dialogue.transliteration: law samahta, lam yasil talabee ba3d.
dialogue.english: Excuse me, my order hasn't arrived yet.

dialogue.speaker: Waiter
dialogue.arabic: آسِف. هَلْ تُرِيدُ أَنْ أُعِيدَ الطَّلَب؟
dialogue.transliteration: aasif. hal tureedu an u3eeda at-talab?
dialogue.english: Sorry. Do you want me to repeat the order?

dialogue.speaker: Rami
dialogue.arabic: نَعَمْ، لَوْ سَمَحْتَ. نُرِيدُ نَفْسَ الطَّلَب.
dialogue.transliteration: na3am, law samahta. nureedu nafsa at-talab.
dialogue.english: Yes, please. We want the same order.

response.english: Yes, I'll have a plate of hummus.

pair.arabic: هَلْ يُمْكِنُ أَنْ أَحْصُلَ عَلَى كُوبِ مَاء؟
pair.transliteration: hal yumkinu an a7sula 3alaa koobi maa2?
pair.english: Can I have a glass of water?

lessons.culture: Ordering in Fusha is done with the future سَآخُذُ and wish words like أُرِيدُ, never with a bare command. Saying مِنْ فَضْلِكَ and شُكْرًا with every request keeps the meal friendly.

exercises.prompt: The waiter asks: 'هَلْ أَنْتُمْ جَاهِزُونَ لِلطَّلَب؟'. Say yes and order hummus and fattoush.

too_formal.item: إِي، رَح آخُد صَحْن حُمُّص وَفَتُّوش

exercises.tip: سَآخُذُ is 'I will take', a natural way to order.

exercises.prompt: The waiter asks: 'هَلْ تُرِيدُونَ شَيْئًا آخَر؟'. Say that is enough, thanks.
exercises.tip: يَكْفِي means 'it is enough'.

exercises.prompt: Complete: '_____ بَصَل، مِنْ فَضْلِكَ.' (Without onion, please.)
exercises.tip: Use بِدُونِ before the thing you do not want.

exercises.prompt: Complete: 'لَمْ يَصِلْ طَلَبِي _____.' (My order hasn't arrived yet.)
exercises.tip: With لَمْ, بَعْد at the end means 'yet'.

exercises.prompt: Translate into Fusha: 'Extra bread, please.'
exercises.tip: إِضَافِيّ means 'additional'.

exercises.prompt: Translate: 'We want the same order.'
exercises.tip: نُرِيدُ is 'we want'; نَفْسَ means 'the same'.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence asks for a glass of water?
options: هَلْ يُمْكِنُ أَنْ أَحْصُلَ عَلَى كُوبِ مَاء؟
exercises.answer: هَلْ يُمْكِنُ أَنْ أَحْصُلَ عَلَى كُوبِ مَاء؟
accepted: هَلْ يُمْكِنُ أَنْ أَحْصُلَ عَلَى كُوبِ مَاء؟
هل يمكن أن أحصل على كوب ماء؟
hal yumkinu an a7sula 3alaa koobi maa2?
هل يمكن ان احصل على كوب ماء
exercises.tip: كُوب is a glass or cup and مَاء is water.

exercises.prompt: You want the waiter to hurry. What do you say?
exercises.tip: بِسُرْعَة means 'with speed', quickly.

exercises.prompt: Put the pieces in order: 'وَهَذَا / هَذَا / أُرِيدُ'.
exercises.tip: Point at the first dish, then add the second with وَ.

exercises.prompt: Put the pieces in order: 'لَهَا / لِي / هَذَا الطَّبَقُ / وَهَذَا'.
accepted: haadha at-tabaqu lee wa haadha lahaa
exercises.tip: لِي is 'for me' and لَهَا is 'for her'.

dialogue.speaker: Rami
dialogue.english: Excuse me, the bill please.

dialogue.speaker: Waiter
dialogue.english: Certainly. Here you are.

dialogue.speaker: Rami
dialogue.english: How much is the bill?

dialogue.speaker: Waiter
dialogue.english: Two thousand five hundred pounds.

dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.english: Shall we split the bill?

dialogue.speaker: Rami
dialogue.english: No, I'm paying today.

dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.english: Thank you very much, Rami.

dialogue.speaker: Rami
dialogue.english: Do you take cash or card?

dialogue.speaker: Waiter
dialogue.english: We take both.

dialogue.speaker: Rami
dialogue.english: Is the tip included in the bill?

dialogue.speaker: Waiter
dialogue.english: No, it is not included.

dialogue.speaker: Rami
dialogue.arabic: الْبَاقِي لَكَ. تُسْلَمُ يَدَاكَ، كَانَ الطَّعَام لَذِيذ.
dialogue.transliteration: al-baaqee laka. tuslamu yadaaka, kaana at-ta3aamu ladheedh.
dialogue.english: Keep the change. Bless your hands, the food was delicious.

pair.english: Do you take cash or card?

lessons.culture: Insisting on paying is part of Arab hospitality, so a polite tug-of-war over the bill is normal. تُسْلَمُ يَدَاكَ, 'may your hands be safe', is the warm way to praise the cook.

exercises.prompt: Your friend says: 'هَلْ نَتَقَاسَمُ الْحِسَاب؟'. Insist on paying.
exercises.tip: سَأَدْفَعُ is 'I will pay'.

exercises.prompt: Someone says to you: 'تُسْلَمُ يَدَاكَ'. Reply politely.
exercises.tip: It wishes the eater pleasure and health.

exercises.prompt: Complete: 'الْحِسَاب، _____ فَضْلِكَ.' (The bill, please.)
exercises.tip: مِنْ فَضْلِكَ is 'from your kindness', please.

exercises.prompt: Complete: 'الْبَاقِي _____.' (Keep the change.)
exercises.tip: الْبَاقِي is 'the rest'; لَكَ means 'for you'.

exercises.prompt: Translate into Fusha: 'How much is the bill?'
exercises.tip: يَبْلُغُ means 'it amounts to'.

exercises.prompt: Translate: 'Is there a discount today?'
exercises.tip: خَصْم is 'discount'.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence asks whether they take cash or card?
exercises.tip: أَمْ joins two options in a question: 'or'.

exercises.prompt: You want a receipt. Which question do you ask?
exercises.tip: الْإِيصَال is the receipt.

exercises.prompt: Put the pieces in order: 'الْحِسَاب؟ / يَبْلُغُ / كَمْ'.
exercises.tip: كَمْ opens the question, the bill closes it.

exercises.prompt: Put the pieces in order: 'سَأَدْفَعُ / الْيَوْم / أَنَا'.
exercises.tip: Who pays, will pay, when.

phrases.transliteration: ureedu burjar dajaaj wa bataata maqliyya

phrases.arabic: هَلْ تَأْكُلُ هُنَا أَمْ تَأْخُذُهُ مَعَكَ؟
phrases.transliteration: hal ta2kulu hunaa am ta2khudhuhu ma3aka?

phrases.arabic: أَيَّ حَجْم تُرِيد، صَغِير أَمْ مُتَوَسِّط أَمْ كَبِير؟
phrases.transliteration: ayya 7ajm tureed, sagheer am mutawassit am kabeer?

dialogue.speaker: Cashier
dialogue.english: Welcome. What would you like?

dialogue.speaker: Rami
dialogue.transliteration: ureedu burjar dajaaj wa bataata maqliyya.
dialogue.english: I'd like a chicken burger and fries.

dialogue.speaker: Cashier
dialogue.arabic: أَيَّ حَجْم تُرِيد، صَغِير أَمْ مُتَوَسِّط أَمْ كَبِير؟
dialogue.transliteration: ayya 7ajm tureed, sagheer am mutawassit am kabeer?
dialogue.english: Which size do you want, small, medium or large?

dialogue.speaker: Rami
dialogue.arabic: كُولَا كَبِيرَة، مِنْ فَضْلِكَ. بِدُونِ ثَلْج، مِنْ فَضْلِكَ.
dialogue.transliteration: koolaa kabeera, min fadlika. bidooni thalj, min fadlika.
dialogue.english: A large cola, please. Without ice, please.

dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.english: Do you have a kids' meal?

dialogue.speaker: Cashier
dialogue.english: Yes, it comes with a small gift.

dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.english: Is the meat halal?

dialogue.speaker: Cashier
dialogue.arabic: نَعَمْ، كُلُّ لُحُومِنَا حَلَال. هَلْ تَأْكُلُونَ هُنَا أَمْ تَأْخُذُونَهُ مَعَكُمْ؟
dialogue.transliteration: na3am, kullu luhoomina 7alaal. hal ta2kuloona hunaa am ta2khudhoonahu ma3akum?
dialogue.english: Yes, all our meat is halal. Are you eating here or taking it with you?

dialogue.speaker: Rami
dialogue.arabic: لِلْأَخْذِ، مِنْ فَضْلِكَ. كَمْ سَيَسْتَغْرِقُ الطَّلَب؟
dialogue.transliteration: lil-2akhdh, min fadlika. kam sayastaghriqu at-talab?
dialogue.english: To take away, please. How long will the order take?

dialogue.speaker: Cashier
dialogue.english: Only five minutes.

dialogue.speaker: Rami
dialogue.arabic: شُكْرًا. مِنْ فَضْلِكَ، ضَعْهُ فِي كِيس.
dialogue.transliteration: shukran. min faDlik, Da3hu fee kees.
dialogue.english: Thanks. Please put it in a bag.

dialogue.speaker: Cashier
dialogue.english: Here you are, enjoy your meal.

response.english: I'd like a burger and fries.

pair.arabic: هَلْ تَأْكُلُونَ هُنَا أَمْ تَأْخُذُونَهُ مَعَكُمْ؟
pair.transliteration: hal ta2kuloona hunaa am ta2khudhoonahu ma3akum?
pair.english: Are you eating here or taking it with you?

response.english: Yes, all our meat is halal.

pair.english: How long will the order take?

lessons.culture: Fast-food counters in the Arab world are quick and friendly, and the first question is usually whether the order is to eat in or to take away. Many chains are fully halal, but asking هَلِ اللَّحْم حَلَال؟ is normal and never rude. A meal, وَجْبَة, usually comes as a set with fries and a drink.

exercises.prompt: Translate into Fusha: 'I'd like a chicken burger and fries.'
accepted: ureedu burjar dajaaj wa bataata maqliyya
exercises.tip: أُرِيدُ is 'I want', polite when ordering.

exercises.prompt: Translate: 'Without ice, please.'
exercises.tip: بِدُونِ means 'without'.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence asks whether the meat is halal?
options: هَلْ تَأْكُلُ هُنَا أَمْ تَأْخُذُهُ مَعَكَ؟
exercises.tip: حَلَال means 'permitted', the word for halal food.

exercises.prompt: You want your food to take away. What do you say?
exercises.tip: لِلْأَخْذِ is 'for taking'.

exercises.prompt: Put the pieces in order: 'فَضْلِكَ / مِنْ / كَبِيرَة، / كُولَا'.
exercises.tip: The drink first, then the polite word.

exercises.prompt: Put the pieces in order: 'الطَّلَب؟ / سَيَسْتَغْرِقُ / كَمْ'.
exercises.tip: سَيَسْتَغْرِقُ is 'it will take' (time).

exercises.prompt: Complete: 'أَيَّ _____ تُرِيد، صَغِير أَمْ كَبِير؟' (Which size do you want?)
exercises.tip: حَجْم is 'size'.

exercises.prompt: Complete: 'هَلْ عِنْدَكُمْ _____ لِلْأَطْفَال؟' (Do you have a kids' meal?)
exercises.tip: وَجْبَة is a meal.

exercises.prompt: The cashier asks: 'هَلْ تَأْكُلُونَ هُنَا أَمْ تَأْخُذُونَهُ مَعَكُمْ؟'. You want takeaway.
exercises.tip: Answer with the short phrase, then مِنْ فَضْلِكَ.

exercises.prompt: The cashier asks: 'مَاذَا تُرِيدُونَ؟'. Order a burger and fries.
exercises.tip: Start with أُرِيدُ, 'I want'.

dialogue.speaker: Yusuf
dialogue.english: Thank you for the invitation.

dialogue.speaker: Host
dialogue.english: Welcome. Please, sit down.

dialogue.speaker: Yusuf
dialogue.english: I am honoured by your invitation.

dialogue.speaker: Host
dialogue.english: Bismillah, please begin.

dialogue.speaker: Yusuf
dialogue.arabic: بِسْمِ اللهِ. مَا أَطْيَبَ هَذَا الطَّعَام!
dialogue.english: Bismillah. How delicious this food is!

dialogue.speaker: Host
dialogue.english: Please, take some more.

dialogue.speaker: Yusuf
dialogue.english: Please pass me the water.

dialogue.speaker: Host
dialogue.english: Here you are.

dialogue.speaker: Yusuf
dialogue.english: Thank Allah, I'm full.

dialogue.speaker: Host
dialogue.english: Shall we have tea after the meal?

dialogue.speaker: Yusuf
dialogue.arabic: نَعَمْ، وَجَزَاكُمُ اللهُ خَيْرًا. الْمَرَّة الْقَادِمَة عَلَيْنَا.
dialogue.transliteration: na3am, wa jazaakumu llaahu khayran. al-marra al-qaadima 3alaynaa.
dialogue.english: Yes, and may Allah reward you well. Next time it's on us.

dialogue.speaker: Host
dialogue.english: You are welcome any time.

pair.english: Shall we have tea after the meal?

lessons.culture: A guest says بِسْمِ اللهِ before the first bite and eats with the right hand. The host will urge you to take more, so refusing once and then accepting a little is polite. Thank the host with جَزَاكُمُ اللهُ خَيْرًا, and the answer is وَإِيَّاكُمْ.

exercises.prompt: Translate into Fusha: 'Thank you for the invitation.'
exercises.tip: عَلَى means 'for' here: thanks on the invitation.

exercises.prompt: Translate: 'How delicious this food is!'
exercises.tip: مَا أَطْيَبَ is the 'how...!' pattern.

exercises.prompt: What do you say before you start eating?
exercises.tip: Bismillah means 'in the name of Allah'.

exercises.prompt: You want the water. Which sentence do you say?
exercises.tip: نَاوِلْنِي means 'hand me'.

exercises.prompt: Put the pieces in order: 'الدَّعْوَة / عَلَى / شُكْرًا'.
exercises.tip: Thanks first, then what for.

exercises.prompt: Put the pieces in order: 'الطَّعَام؟ / بَعْدَ / الشَّايَ / نَشْرَبُ / هَلْ'.
exercises.tip: بَعْدَ means 'after'.

exercises.prompt: Complete: 'شُكْرًا عَلَى _____.' (Thank you for the invitation.)
exercises.tip: الدَّعْوَة is 'the invitation'.

exercises.prompt: Complete: 'جَزَاكُمُ اللهُ _____.' (May Allah reward you well.)
exercises.tip: خَيْرًا is 'good'.

exercises.prompt: The host says: 'تَفَضَّلْ، خُذْ أَكْثَر.'. You are full.
exercises.tip: Thank Allah first, then say you are full.

exercises.prompt: A guest says to you: 'جَزَاكُمُ اللهُ خَيْرًا.'. Reply.
exercises.tip: It means 'and you too'.

challenge.title: A meal out
challenge.instructions: Write a short conversation in Fusha between a waiter and two guests. Order drinks, ask about the menu, order a meal with one change, and then settle the bill and thank the waiter.
required_elements: a question about the menu or a dish
a meal ordered with a change such as without onion
a request such as extra bread or water
a question about the bill or how to pay

dialogue.speaker: Waiter
dialogue.arabic: أَهْلًا وَسَهْلًا. مَاذَا تُحِبُّونَ أَنْ تَشْرَبُوا؟
dialogue.transliteration: ahlan wa sahlan. maadha tu7ibboona an tashraboo?
dialogue.english: Welcome. What would you like to drink?

dialogue.speaker: Rami
dialogue.english: Coffee with no sugar, please.

dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.transliteration: wa anaa shaay bin-na3naa3, min fadlika.
dialogue.english: And I'll have mint tea, please.

dialogue.speaker: Rami
dialogue.english: Is there a dish of the day?

dialogue.speaker: Waiter
dialogue.arabic: نَعَمْ، أُرْز بِالدَّجَاج. وَهُوَ غَيْرُ حَارّ.
dialogue.transliteration: na3am, urz bid-dajaaj. wa huwa ghayru 7aarr.
dialogue.english: Yes, rice with chicken. And it is not spicy.

dialogue.speaker: Rami
dialogue.arabic: سَآخُذُ طَبَقَ الْيَوْم، وَخُبْز إِضَافِيّ، مِنْ فَضْلِكَ.
dialogue.transliteration: sa2aakhudhu tabaqa al-yawm, wa khubz idaafee, min fadlika.
dialogue.english: I'll have the dish of the day, and extra bread, please.

dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.english: I want fattoush without onion.

dialogue.speaker: Waiter
dialogue.english: Certainly. Do you want anything else?

dialogue.speaker: Rami
dialogue.english: Thanks, that's enough. The bill later.

dialogue.speaker: Rami
dialogue.arabic: الْحِسَاب، مِنْ فَضْلِكَ. هَلْ تَقْبَلُونَ الْبِطَاقَة؟
dialogue.transliteration: al-7isaab, min fadlika. hal taqbaloona al-bitaaqa?
dialogue.english: The bill, please. Do you take cards?

dialogue.speaker: Waiter
dialogue.english: Yes, here you are.

dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.english: Bless your hands, the food was delicious.
